page.layout: One page of running text in one column. In the right margin, beside the lines, are marginal notes: "De lacte humano memorabilia." (several lines), "Lac nigrum." (two lines) and "Pulticulae lactariae." (two lines). The running head and page number are at the top.

p.i: ceat, asininum ipsis dari conveniet. Hac Galen.

Conferre quoque aliquid & candori mulierum cuti existimantur. Poppæa Domitii Neronis coniux quingentas secum per omnia trahens asinas fœtas asininum nobilitauit, balneorum etiam solio totum corpus illo lacte maceranit, sic candi-dieri cutē extendiq; existimans. Sed longe asinino in pithisi, humanum præstantius est, nam pecu-De lacte humano memorabilia.liariter extenuatis plurimum & frugi alimen-tum confert, corporisq; robur restituit. In expe-rimentis sunt, qui iam tabe & atrophia cofumti solo lacte ex vegeta & florentis mulieris uberibus susto sunt refti uti. Sic Dauid septuagenarius cū senili torpore frigeret, nec pellib. cooperiens inca-lesceret, in speciati decoris puella amplexib° caste condormiuit, vt eius calore robur stomachi soue retur. Equino septentrionis gentes quaedam in cibis & potu viuntur, quod hic meminisse lestore volo, sicut & illud, quod in Ponto fluviu Asiaces ri-gat campos, in quibus pastanigro lacte equa gen-Lac ni-grum.tem alant. Lactaria pulticula, (quæ fiunt ex lacte similagini misto, inq; sartagine decosto, fre-quentissq; cum spatula versato in lenta pruna, sPulticu-læ lacta-riæ. ne sartigini adhærescat, vsq; ad modicam crassi-tudinem, & donec crusta tenui obducatur, ) apud nostratus quasdam fœminas Principes in summis delitiis habentur, sunt enim suauissimi saporis, & odoris, si addatur crocus, optimiq; ac firmi nutrimenti. Sofistratum nullo cibo & potu alio quam lacte toto vita sue curriculo vsum fu-isse

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "ceat" is a fragment from the previous page, left as printed. "lacte" in the text is printed with a ligature that could also be read as "laste"; read as lacte from the margin note. "susto sunt refti uti" and "Ponto fluviu Asiaces" are uncertain. The running head and the page number "573" are read from a faint scan. The final word "isse" is partly cut off at the edge of the scan. The first paragraph is continued from the previous page. The paragraph breaks follow the indents and the short line after "Galen.". Printed text is set throughout in italic, so the whole page is marked as italic.
